narrative.title: Sizing a Square Server Rack Footprint
narrative.scenario: A datacenter planner receives a floor area in square units and wants the side of the largest square rack cluster that fits exactly or smaller. When the area is not a perfect square, the planner floors the side length. Search the side-length range directly rather than calling a floating-point library routine.
narrative.inputFormat: A single long integer x, the area.
narrative.outputFormat: floor(sqrt(x)), the largest integer whose square does not exceed x.
constraints: The result must be exact integer arithmetic, not floating point

testCases.explanation: 2 squared is 4, which fits, while 3 squared overshoots 5 - so the floored side is 2.
The area is a perfect square and the side is exactly 2.

hintLevels: Level 1: The predicate 'does this side fit the area' is monotonic - once a side fails, every larger side fails too.
Level 2: Search sides from 1 up to x, carrying the best fitting side as the answer and probing the midpoint each round.
Level 3: Squaring the midpoint can overflow narrow integer types, so widen it, and an exact hit should return immediately rather than continuing to search.
